title: Why are most traffic lights red, yellow, and green?

lines.text: Why does almost every country on Earth use red, yellow, and green for traffic signals?
lines.caps: Why are traffic *lights | red, yellow, and *green?

lines.text: The system dates back to nineteenth-century British railway signals.
Red has the longest wavelength of any visible light spectrum.
lines.caps: Red has the *longest | wavelength of *visible light

lines.text: This means red scatters the least in rain and dense fog, allowing drivers to spot danger from the farthest distance.
lines.caps: Scatters least in *fog | so you spot *danger early

lines.text: Railroads originally used clear white light for 'go', but drivers mistook stars or streetlamps for signals.
lines.caps: White was used for *go | but caused disastrous *train crashes!

lines.text: So engineers adopted green for safety, and later added bright yellow as a transition warning.
That nineteenth-century railroad color code keeps hundreds of millions of drivers safe today.
lines.caps: Railroad color code | keeping *millions safe | *every day!
